method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading; exact macro, identifier, token and formula comparison; and replay of the isomorphism and compactness arguments, including the cardinality conclusion. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Non-standard arithmetic structures and numbers, an independence exercise for Q's first three axioms, an integer-domain counterexample and the compactness construction of an enumerable non-standard model of true arithmetic.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A structure is non-standard exactly when it is not isomorphic to N. Its standard numbers are the values of standard numerals; any other carrier elements are non-standard, and their existence prevents an isomorphism from N from being surjective.
samples.checks: The element/value quantifiers, induction identity and surjectivity contradiction all keep their original directions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercise asks for separate structures witnessing independence patterns among Q1 through Q3. An ordinary integer structure is non-standard because negative integers are not numeral values, but it is not a model of true arithmetic because zero has an integer predecessor.
samples.checks: Every satisfaction and non-satisfaction mark in the three requested patterns is preserved, as is the counterexample sentence.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Add a constant c required to differ from every standard numeral. Every finite subset is modeled by N with c assigned one more than the largest excluded numeral; the case with no such inequality is handled directly. Compactness gives a model, forgetting c leaves a non-standard model of true arithmetic, and Downward Löwenheim–Skolem supplies the claimed enumerable size.
samples.checks: The slash-equality constraints remain inequalities, the witness is interpreted in the expanded structure, all finite-subset cases are covered and the cardinality step now follows from an explicitly named available theorem.

source_observations: T281 now covers the source-defined standard/non-standard contrast for models, elements and the numbers those elements represent.
The frozen witness formula takes c's interpretation in the reduct M even though c exists only in the expansion M-superscript-c; OLFOL-031 records the corrected structure argument.

The frozen compactness proof omits both the finite-subset case with no c-inequality and the step proving the proposition's enumerable cardinality claim; OLFOL-033 and OLFOL-032 record the bounded prose additions.
All unaffected macros, identifiers, controlled tokens and formulas match the frozen source; the corrected witness formula passes the documented source-correction projection.
